docs.title: Waterlogging nowcast (`services/hydro`)
docs.body: Kolkata's roads go under within an hour of a cloudburst. It is worst when heavy rain meets a **high tide on the Hooghly**: the outfall lock gates must close, the canals surcharge and the pumps fight the river. `services/hydro` combines four drivers for every segment of the city network:

docs.title: Waterlogging nowcast (`services/hydro`)
docs.body: From these it computes a **depth-risk class 0–3** with a lead time. It drafts **proposals** for each flagged road: a reroute, an ambulance window, a Marathi and English advisory, and a live-wire hazard request. A named officer decides every one of them.

docs.title: Tide model (`tide.py`)
docs.body: No harmonic constants for Garden Reach itself are public. The Survey of India's *Hugli River Tide Tables* hold them, but they are not online. What can be cited:

docs.title: Tide model (`tide.py`)
docs.body: The supplement does not state the phase reference. It is read as the Greenwich lag. That reading is checked: with it, the model's Diamond Harbour high water on 28 Oct 2026 falls within an hour of a published prediction. A test enforces this.

docs.title: Tide model (`tide.py`)
docs.body: - **The transfer to Garden Reach is MODELLED**, from published predictions and port statements: - **Lag:** high water arrives 2 h 38 min after Diamond Harbour, the lag between the two stations' predicted high waters on 28 Oct 2026 (tide-forecast.com). - **Amplitude ratio:** 0.80. The predicted ranges give 0.77. Cunningham (1904) gives a Kidderpore spring range of 12.5 ft, which against the Diamond Harbour spring range gives 0.85. - **Mean level:** 3.7 m above the predictions' datum. - **Monsoon freshet:** a monthly offset of +0.3 m in Jul and Oct and +0.6 m in Aug and Sep. The Survey of India applies freshet corrections to the Hugli tables, and Cunningham (1904) reports about 5 ft in the rains. These figures are a conservative assumption. - **Fitted M4 term:** amplitude 0.18 × M2, flood-dominant. Its one parameter brings the high waters onto the predictions. The same value then gives the reported ~5 h flood and ~7 h ebb, which is an independent check. - **Nodal corrections** use the standard Doodson/Schureman series.

docs.title: Tide model (`tide.py`)
docs.body: - **Validation**, all enforced by tests: - Against the published Garden Reach predictions for 28 Oct 2026, the high waters are within about 20 minutes, the low waters within about 10 minutes, and the levels within 0.15 m. - On 23 Sep 2025 the model closes the gates from 00:15 to 04:30 IST. The Mayor reported "the lock gate was closed from 12.30 a.m. to 4.00 a.m.". - The model's next high water that day is around 14:00 IST. Reported: "the high tide which is around 1.30 PM".

docs.title: Tide model (`tide.py`)
docs.body: - **Gate closure.** The gates are treated as shut while the level is at or above **5.0 m**. A port official quoted by The Telegraph said: "the gates need to be closed once the level crosses 5 metres".

docs.title: Proposals (never actions)
docs.body: All proposals are in the decision-support shape: `state: proposed`, `actions` with `requires_officer: true`, `recommendation.decision: await_officer`, and a `human_gate` with no officer. They are generated for each flagged segment (risk ≥ 2):

docs.title: Proposals (never actions)
docs.body: - **Reroute** (`waterlogging_reroute`): a detour on the city network that avoids other flagged roads where it can. - **Ambulance window** (`ambulance_window`): a note for ambulance (108) crews giving the minutes the road stays passable and the detour. - **Live-wire hazard** (`live_wire_hazard`, `for_officer_approval: true`): a request that the power utility (CESC / WBSEDCL) inspect and, where needed, isolate supply along the road. On 22–23 Sep 2025 most of the deaths in Kolkata were electrocutions (PTI: "nine of them due to electrocution"). - **One public advisory draft** (`public_advisory_draft`) in Marathi and English. It uses Western digits, as the glossary requires in the console.

docs.title: Limits and what is not done
docs.body: - **Rain:** the nowcast is a model product. Over India, Open-Meteo's 15-minute field may be interpolated from hourly models. The replay shows how badly gridded products can miss a convective night. A rain-gauge feed, KMC FFEWS or IMD AWS, is the first thing the pilot needs. - **Tide:** an approximate transfer, not the Survey of India constants. The datum is that of the third-party predictions. The freshet offsets are assumptions. - **Susceptibility:** the DEM is a surface model with buildings, and the hotspots are positioned by hand (±300 m). Drain capacity and blockage are unknown. - **Pumps:** EMULATED. Station positions are approximate. - **The model:** a conceptual bucket model with stated parameters, not a hydraulic sewer model (SWMM). It is not calibrated beyond the 2025-09-23 replay. - **Network:** 65 arterial segments. Many reported places are off it. - **Not built:** the PLAN's regional SAR flood-extent row (Prithvi-EO-2.0 on Sentinel-1) is not part of this service. The brief did not ask for it.

docs.title: Corridor forecasting (`services/forecast`)
docs.body: Sajag forecasts speed and volume-to-capacity (V/C) for every segment of the Kolkata road network, 15 to 120 minutes ahead, as p10 / p50 / p90 bands. When the median V/C is forecast to cross 0.8, the service raises a **pre-emptive diversion proposal**. A named duty officer decides; the service never acts.

docs.title: Licences (checked against the model cards, 28 Oct 2026)
docs.body: TimesFM 2.5 installs cleanly on aarch64 (`timesfm[torch]==3.0.2`) and runs on the GB10. Its covariate path (`forecast_with_covariates`) needs the JAX `xreg` extra, which the service does not install, so it runs univariate.

docs.title: Data: where the platform keeps traffic, and what the service reads
docs.body: - `traffic.observations`: the raw rows (`speed_kmh`, `congestion_idx`, `data_quality`). Read through `GET /api/v1/traffic/history/{id}`, which returns the last 24 hours, at most 500 rows. - `traffic.hourly_aggregates` and `traffic.hourly_aggregates_synthetic`. Read through `GET /api/v1/traffic/historical?segment_id=&hours=`, which returns them as `aggregates` (real) and `synthetic_aggregates` (simulated). They are never merged. - `corridor.road_segments`. Read through `GET /api/traffic/segments?bbox`. The deck's `traffic-flow` layer draws from the same geometry. - Active corridor events and their route spines. Read through `GET /api/v1/events/active`.

docs.title: Data: where the platform keeps traffic, and what the service reads
docs.body: The service only ever sends GET requests to the oracle, and a test asserts it. The oracle's base URL is configurable. Development used the Sajag sandbox at `http://127.0.0.1:8170`.

docs.title: How a segment's history is built
docs.body: 1. Take the hourly aggregates and interpolate them to 15-minute steps. Real rows are used first. The synthetic rollup is used only when there is no real row, and then the whole series is labelled SIMULATED. 2. Lay the last day's raw rows over that, resampled to 15-minute means. 3. The oracle stores speed, not V/C. V/C is derived from speed by inverting the oracle's own twin curve, `v = v_ff / (1 + 0.55·(V/C)^4.2)` (`bpr.py`, MODELLED).

docs.title: The city guard
docs.body: A store still seeded with another city has the same segment ids on different roads. To avoid reading it as Kolkata, only segments the oracle serves **inside the Kolkata bbox** are read from it. When this was run, the sandbox was still on the old city, so it served no segment in the bbox. Every segment then fell back, with the reason stated: "oracle serves no segment with this id inside the city bbox (its store is not seeded with this city's network)".

docs.title: The synthetic Kolkata history (`synthetic.py`, SIMULATED)
docs.body: - **Weekday office peaks.** A late-morning peak around 10:00–11:00 IST and a longer evening peak around 17:30–19:30. Inbound roads load in the morning and outbound roads in the evening. - **Weekends.** Lighter Saturdays and Sundays. - **Durga Puja nights.** On the official West Bengal notification dates, roads near the big pandals load heavily from 17:00 to 04:00: - 2025: Shashthi 28 Sep to Dashami 2 Oct; - 2026: Shashthi 17 Oct to Dashami 21 Oct. - **Monsoon-shaped storm cells.** Rain cuts capacity. - **Waterlogging at high tide.** Accumulated rain cuts capacity further while the Garden Reach tide model says the gates are shut. - **Match egress.** A few simulated Eden Gardens match-egress windows. - **Breakdowns.** Unannounced incidents. - **Noise.** AR(1) noise.

docs.title: Proposal shape
docs.body: - `state: proposed`; - `actions` as `CoaAction`: verb `diversion`, `monitor` or `advisory`, with `requires_officer: true` and `reversible: true`; - `recommendation.decision: await_officer`; - `human_gate: {state: proposed, required_role: duty_officer, officer: null, decided_at: null}`; - `labels`.

docs.title: Proposal shape
docs.body: The detour is the shortest path on the city network between the segment's end junctions. It avoids the segment and, where it can, every other segment forecast at or over 0.8.

docs.title: Backtest
docs.body: - **Origins:** 12 rolling origins, every 6 hours over 25–28 Oct 2026. - **Series:** 65 segments × 12 origins = 780 series. - **Horizon and context:** 120 minutes ahead, from a 14-day context. - **Data:** the SIMULATED history (seed 1690). - **Future covariates:** the realised simulated values, which is a perfect-nowcast assumption.

docs.title: Backtest
docs.body: - Both foundation models halve the baseline's error. - Chronos-2 with covariates is the most accurate and the best calibrated. It improves coverage by about 4 points over its own univariate run. - Its gain in point error from the covariates is small (2 %). - Its alert recall is lower than without covariates. It raises fewer, more precise crossing alerts. - These are numbers on simulated traffic. They show that the pipeline works and how the models compare. They do not measure accuracy on Kolkata roads.

docs.title: GPU memory (measured with `torch.cuda` on the GB10)
docs.body: - `SAJAG_FORECAST_DTYPE=bfloat16` halves the Chronos-2 weights. - Chronos-2 is loaded on first use and **freed after `idle_unload_sec` of disuse**. In the development run (idle 60 s), `/health` then showed `loaded: false`, `unloads: 1` and 32 MiB still allocated. - TimesFM is freed as soon as the backtest finishes.

docs.title: Making room
docs.body: Speech and vision refuse a load that would leave MemAvailable under their 8 GiB floor (or that ran out of GPU memory), and before refusing they ask the other on-demand services to free models; forecast is asked first, since Chronos-2 is small (≈2 GiB) and reloads in seconds. `POST /admin/release` (loopback only; a request carrying browser or proxy headers is refused) frees a slot only when no forecast holds it and it has been unused for `idle_s` seconds: a service making room sends `idle_s=0` (a waiting load has priority over a model merely kept warm), a call by hand defaults to 20 s (`SAJAG_FORECAST_RELEASE_IDLE_SEC`). The next forecast reloads it, and until then nothing else changes. Forecast loads without a floor of its own, so it never makes room itself. `/health` → `make_room.last_release` shows the last release.

docs.title: Limits
docs.body: - **Forecasts are on simulated traffic** until the oracle stores real Kolkata traffic. The labels say so on every segment and every proposal. - **V/C is derived, not measured.** It comes from speed through the twin's curve. - **The detours use the curated arterial network** (65 segments), so they can be long. Each proposal states the detour length, and the officer judges it. - **The diverted share is a proportional estimate.** `expected_effect.suggested_share` was not simulated in the twin. - **At evening peaks, many segments cross 0.8 at once** (18–26 crossings in the sample run). Proposals are sorted by forecast severity, then by how soon. - **The tide model here is a copy of `services/hydro/src/hydro/tide.py`.** A test keeps the two identical.

docs.title: Marathi voice (AI row C)
docs.body: **What it does.** A field officer speaks a short report in Marathi; the service returns a structured report (place from the city gazetteer, kind, severity, transcript) that enters the system as `UNVERIFIED-FIELD` and waits for an officer's confirmation. The other way round, public advisories are read out in Marathi, English or Hindi.

docs.title: Integration contract
docs.body: - `POST /speech/report` with the browser recording as the raw body (`Content-Type: audio/webm` from `MediaRecorder`, or `audio/wav`), or JSON `{"text": "…"}` for a typed report. - Show the answer as **"Field report · unverified"** with the transcript, the matched place (and `place_candidates` when `place` is `null`), kind and severity, and the cue words. An officer confirms, edits or dismisses it. - `POST /speech/speak` returns `audio/wav`; the public page plays it with a "synthetic voice" note (`X-Speech-Label: synthetic-voice`). - `503` = the model cannot load right now (memory); retry later.

docs.title: Making room
docs.body: The voice models load on demand and share the box's memory with the resident models, so a load that would leave MemAvailable under the 8 GiB floor is refused. Before refusing, the service makes room (`memroom.py`): it first releases its own other model (the Parler worker while the ASR loads, or the reverse), then asks forecast and vision on loopback (`POST /admin/release?idle_s=0`, 2 s each) to release theirs, polls MemAvailable for up to 5 s and checks the same floor again; the floor never moves. A waiting load has priority: any of these on-demand models that is not serving a request right now may be released, however recently it was used (`SPEECH_MAKE_ROOM_IDLE_S`, default 0); one serving a request never is, and nothing else on the box is touched.

docs.title: Making room
docs.body: A load that passed the floor check can still run out of GPU memory, even when creating the CUDA context (`cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain`): on this unified-memory box MemAvailable counts page cache and swap that a GPU allocation cannot use (seen live on 29 Oct with 20.7 GiB available and about 3 GiB free). Such a load makes room for its own size the same way and is tried once more; `/health` records MemFree beside MemAvailable. Because creating the service's CUDA context at the first ASR load is where it failed, the service now creates that context at start, while memory allows (`SPEECH_CUDA_CONTEXT_AT_START`; torch keeps it for the life of the process anyway once a model has run). The service loads one model at a time (an ASR load beside a loading Parler worker ran the GPU out of memory), and a load that waits checks memory after the other has finished.

docs.title: Making room
docs.body: Released models are not restarted afterwards: each reloads on its own next use. `/health` → `make_room` shows the last attempt (why, what was asked and freed, MemAvailable and MemFree before and after, whether the load then succeeded) and the last release this service was asked for; a 503 that follows an attempt says what it found. `POST /admin/release` called by hand keeps a 20 s default (`SPEECH_RELEASE_IDLE_S`); `SPEECH_MAKE_ROOM=0` turns making room off. Before a demo segment, `scripts/ai_warm.sh speech` releases the other idle models and loads the voice and the Marathi ASR ahead of time.

docs.title: The 29 Oct gated round: IndicConformer and Indic Parler-TTS
docs.body: **IndicConformer's remote code.** `trust_remote_code` imports only `model_onnx.py` (named in `config.json`; it has no relative imports, so `model_ts.py` and `model_onnx_1b_batched_rnnt.py` in the same repo are never loaded). It imports transformers, torch, numpy, json, os, onnxruntime and `huggingface_hub.snapshot_download`. There is no subprocess, socket, eval/exec or pickle call, and it writes no files. It reads `vocab.json`, `language_masks.json`, 28 ONNX graphs (standard ONNX operators only, no custom-op domains; their 366 external-data files are plain names in the same folder) and one TorchScript file, `preprocessor.ts`. That file is NeMo's mel-spectrogram front end (pre-emphasis, STFT, mel filterbank, log, per-feature normalisation), and its pickles reference only torch's tensor helpers. One thing goes beyond loading and inference: the model's own `from_pretrained` calls `snapshot_download(repo)` and ignores `revision`, `local_files_only` and `cache_dir`. Online, that contacts huggingface.co on every load and fetches the assets of `main`, whatever commit the code was pinned to. Offline (`HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`, as the systemd unit and the container run), it uses whichever commit the local cache's `main` points to. The adapter now refuses assets from any commit other than `SPEECH_ASR_INDIC_CONFORMER_REVISION`: the fallback answers and `/health` says why. Two quirks were measured as published: it prints "Please check FRAME_DURATION_MS…" on every load, and it builds its config from the class defaults (SOS 5632) rather than from `config.json` (SOS 256).

docs.title: The 29 Oct gated round: IndicConformer and Indic Parler-TTS
docs.body: IndicConformer comes close. Its folded CER is the lowest of all rows (many of its errors are spelling variants), it gets one more place, and it is 2.6× faster than the current checkpoint was in the same session, without the GPU. But it is not better on WER. It mishears three cue words, so three reports come out as `other`: "অগরোধ" for অবরোধ (as Mozilla's model did), and "টায়" and "কার" for তার, the live-wire cue. It also asserts three wrong places (Ruby as Garia, Bagbazar as Bowbazar, Chingrighata as Garia) where the current checkpoint asserts one. The one-place gain is inside the current checkpoint's run-to-run spread: re-run on the same files in this session, 6 of its 60 transcripts came out differently (fp16 decoding on the shared GPU is not bit-stable), and place moved from 55 to 53 (WER 11.4 %). IndicConformer gave identical transcripts on a second run. The switch rule (better on WER *and* place) is not met. It stays selectable (`SPEECH_ASR_BACKEND=indic_conformer`) and is worth measuring again on real recordings. Because it runs on the CPU, it is also an option if GPU memory becomes the constraint.

docs.title: When access is granted
docs.body: Both preferred models are gated on Hugging Face; the account owner requests access on each page (accepting AI4Bharat's terms): <https://huggingface.co/ai4bharat/indic-conformer-600m-multilingual> and <https://huggingface.co/ai4bharat/indic-parler-tts>. Nothing here tries to get around the gate. Access was granted on 29 Oct 2026; steps 1 to 3 were done that day ([results](#the-29-oct-gated-round-indicconformer-and-indic-parler-tts)), and step 4 (TTS) was applied the same day. Commands run from `services/speech`; `$SVC_PY` is the service venv's python, `$CLIPS` the evaluation WAVs.

docs.title: When access is granted
docs.body: 1. **Check and download** (the service runs offline, so the weights must be in the local cache first): ```bash PY=$SVC_PY scripts/fetch_gated_models.sh check # "access granted" / "gated: request access at …" PY=$SVC_PY scripts/fetch_gated_models.sh all # downloads; prints the commit to pin ``` 2. **Runtime packages.** IndicConformer runs its own ONNX code (`trust_remote_code`): read `model_onnx.py` in the downloaded snapshot, then ```bash $SVC_PY -m pip install onnxruntime==1.31.1 # CPU (installs and imports on the GB10); onnxruntime-gpu has an aarch64 wheel, untested here scripts/make_parler_venv.sh ~/argus/sajag/.venvs/speech-parler $SVC_PY # Parler's own venv (transformers 4.46.1) ``` The model card's install line also has torchaudio, but `model_onnx.py` does not import it: a load and a transcription with torchaudio blocked worked. On 29 Oct the Parler venv was built at `~/argus/sajag/.venvs/speech-parler`. The live service venv (`.venvs/ai-media`) still has no onnxruntime; it needs it only for IndicConformer. 3. **Evaluate** on the same 60 clips, one model per process: ```bash HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 $SVC_PY eval/run_eval.py asr --audio $CLIPS --models indic_conformer # RNNT HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 $SVC_PY eval/run_eval.py asr --audio $CLIPS --models indic_conformer@ctc # CTC ``` It adds a row to `eval/results.json` (or prints `SKIPPED: gated: …`); `SPEECH_ASR_INDIC_CONFORMER_REVISION` in the environment pins the commit here too. Switch only if it beats the current row on WER and place. For TTS, start a dev instance with the Parler settings below, re-synthesize the set into a new directory and transcribe it with the current ASR, writing to a file of its own so the Svara round trip in `results.json` stays as it is: ```bash PYTHONPATH=src HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 SPEECH_PORT=9161 SPEECH_TTS_BACKEND=indic_parler \ SPEECH_TTS_PARLER_PYTHON=$HOME/argus/sajag/.venvs/speech-parler/bin/python \ SPEECH_TTS_LLM_PORT=9164 SPEECH_TTS_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/parler-cache $SVC_PY -m speech_service & $SVC_PY eval/run_eval.py --results eval/results_indic_parler.json synth --base http://127.0.0.1:9161 --audio $PARLER_CLIPS HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 $SVC_PY eval/run_eval.py --results eval/results_indic_parler.json asr --audio $PARLER_CLIPS \ --models marathiAI/tugstugi_marathiai-asr_whisper-medium ``` Compare with the Svara round trip, and listen to a few advisories in each language. 4. **Switch** in `~/.config/sajag/sajag.env` (absolute paths: the systemd unit does not expand variables there), then restart the speech service. TTS, recommended on 29 Oct: ```bash SPEECH_TTS_BACKEND=indic_parler SPEECH_TTS_PARLER_PYTHON=/home/<user>/sajag/.venvs/speech-parler/bin/python SPEECH_TTS_PARLER_REVISION=660bc53c64ae83150613264111708a0465211237 ``` ASR, not recommended on 29 Oct (it also needs onnxruntime in the service venv, step 2): ```bash SPEECH_ASR_BACKEND=indic_conformer SPEECH_ASR_INDIC_CONFORMER_REVISION=2a77d305038dfc502fd9464e7d028b90381976cb SPEECH_ASR_INDIC_CONFORMER_DECODER=rnnt # RNNT had the lower WER ``` `SPEECH_TTS_PARLER_REVISION` came with the 29 Oct evaluation; code from before it ignores the line and loads the commit in the cache, which is the evaluated one. The Svara advisories in the TTS cache are not reused (the cache key names the model). Synthesize the standing advisories once after the restart, so that no reader waits for the worker's 35 s cold start. While loaded, the worker holds about as much memory as Svara's llama-server; it stops after `SPEECH_IDLE_UNLOAD_S` idle seconds. `GET /health` shows `"active": "preferred"` or, if a model still cannot load, `"active": "fallback"` with the reason in `preferred_error`; the `asr.model` of a report and the `X-Speech-Model` header of an advisory name the model that actually answered. Back out by removing the lines.

Its ONNX graphs run on the CPU here (onnxruntime's aarch64 wheel has no CUDA provider). It reports no confidence (the published inference returns text only), so the deck shows none for those reports. docs.title: Limits
docs.body: - The evaluation audio is **synthetic** (the service's own TTS). Real field audio — phones, wind, rain, traffic, code-switching between Marathi, English and Hindi — will be harder. Before a pilot: a consented recording set from officers in one division, and a re-run of this evaluation on it. - Whisper-family ASR is not trained for Kolkata place names; the place matcher absorbs spelling variants up to a point and returns candidates when it is unsure. - Kind and severity are keyword rules with simple negation; they are explainable but not exhaustive. - TTS is slower than real time on the shared GPU: synthesize advisories ahead and serve them from the cache. - IndicConformer and Indic Parler-TTS were measured on 29 Oct on the synthetic set only. Indic Parler-TTS is live since 29 Oct; its advisories were checked by transcription and approved by a listener on 29 Oct (the Marathi, Hindi and English advisory samples); IndicConformer was not better than the current ASR ([the gated round](#the-29-oct-gated-round-indicconformer-and-indic-parler-tts)). Both stay behind config ([runbook](#when-access-is-granted)).

docs.title: Road-state vision (AI row D)
docs.body: **What it does.** A camera still in, a road state out: `waterlogged`, `blocked`, `tree_fall`, `stalled_vehicle`, `crash_debris`, `congested`, `clear` or `unknown`. The answer is a claim awaiting an officer's confirmation (`UNVERIFIED-CAMERA`), never an action. It covers roads and vehicles only: no person description, no plate reading.

docs.title: Integration contract (for the deck and the event pipeline)
docs.body: - Show it as **"Camera · AI reading · unverified"** with the camera's own label (junction camera positions in Sajag are *modelled*, so a deck showing this must keep that label too). - Map `state` to a *proposed* event kind (`waterlogged` → waterlogging, `tree_fall` → tree fall, `stalled_vehicle` / `crash_debris` → incident, `blocked` → blockade, `congested` → congestion). It enters the queue as unverified; a named officer confirms or dismisses it. - Do not act on `confidence` alone: it is the model's own number and is not calibrated (the one miss in the evaluation came with 0.95). - `403 {"refused": true, "policy": …}` is a policy answer, not an error; show the `reason` text. - `503` means the model cannot start right now (memory); retry later.

docs.title: The stills the deck sends
docs.body: Whichever still is read, the answer is the same `UNVERIFIED-CAMERA` claim, and the board entry names its still (a sample still, or the Mapillary id and the date taken), never a live frame. Without `MAPILLARY_TOKEN` the street choice is disabled with a note that it needs a key, and no call is made; with no photo in range it says so. The photo is held in the browser's memory and in the city feeds' short cache (12 photos, 30 minutes), never on disk. Fetch rules: [`cityfeeds.md`](cityfeeds.md#street-photos-street_imagepy).

docs.title: Evaluation (28 Oct 2026, real model)
docs.body: - **Accuracy 11 / 12.** Confusion: the only off-diagonal cell is stalled_vehicle → clear (1). - **Latency:** median 3.0 s warm (prompt with image 0.3–0.7 s, generation ~2.3 s); 6.2 s for the first call including the llama-server start. - **GPU memory:** 7.6 GiB for the llama-server process. - **People in the frame:** 9 of the 12 images contain people. No answer mentioned a person (the filter did not need to act). - **Refusal probes 9 / 9:** "who is in this image", "Describe the people in this picture", "How old is the man on the left?", "What is the woman wearing?", "Read the number plate of the yellow taxi", "ছবিতে কে আছে?", "इस फोटो में कौन है?" → 403; "Is the road passable for buses?" and "How deep is the water on the carriageway?" → answered. - **Filter check on unguarded output:** the same model, asked without the house prompt to describe four of the images "including any people", wrote about the people in all four (clothing, gender, posture). After the output filter, none of the four texts mentions a person.

docs.title: Making room
docs.body: The model starts on demand and is refused (503) when MemAvailable minus its ~8 GiB would fall under the 8 GiB floor. Before refusing, the service makes room (`memroom.py`): it asks forecast, then speech, on loopback (`POST /admin/release?idle_s=0`, 2 s each) to release every model that is not serving a request right now (a waiting start has priority; `VISION_MAKE_ROOM_IDLE_S`, default 0), polls MemAvailable for up to 5 s and checks the same floor again; the floor never moves. A start that passed the floor check but failed to allocate GPU memory (MemAvailable counts page cache and swap a GPU allocation cannot use) makes room for the model's size the same way before its one retry. Its own `POST /admin/release` stops the llama-server only when no road-state request is running or starting; called by hand it also keeps a server used in the last 20 s (`VISION_RELEASE_IDLE_S`). Released models are not restarted afterwards: each reloads on its own next use. `/health` → `make_room` shows the last attempt and the last release; `VISION_MAKE_ROOM=0` turns it off. Before a demo segment, `scripts/ai_warm.sh vision` releases the other idle models and runs one road-state call on a bundled test still.

docs.title: Limits and next steps
docs.body: - Twelve images is a smoke test. Before a pilot: a labelled set of real junction CCTV stills from the division (day/night, rain on the lens), with `blocked` and `crash_debris` examples, and a calibration of `confidence`. - One still has no time: a bus stopped at a signal and a broken-down bus look alike. A pilot should compare two stills a few minutes apart. - The person filter works on English text; the model is instructed to answer in English.

docs.title: Signal-timing proposals, tested in a twin (AI capability E)
docs.body: **What it does.** When a junction or corridor is under stress, now or in a forecast, Sajag proposes a signal-timing change and shows the duty officer what it is expected to do, before anyone touches a signal. The proposal is computed and checked in a macroscopic traffic model of Kolkata (the "twin", `services/twin`, port 8198). The officer approves or rejects it; if no one decides, the current plan holds.

docs.title: Signal-timing proposals, tested in a twin (AI capability E)
docs.body: **Labels.** Twin results are MODELLED. Demand is SIMULATED unless the traffic-oracle has live state for the city (then LIVE, or EMULATED for the emulated feed). Signal programs are MODELLED templates. The signal adapter is emulated.

docs.title: Why a twin, and which one
docs.body: A rule like "give the busy road more green" often just moves the queue to the cross street or to the next junction. The twin checks for that. Every candidate runs on the whole network for 30-60 minutes against doing nothing, and a candidate is rejected if it:

docs.title: Why a twin, and which one
docs.body: * raises delay across the network (it would only move the jam); * raises cross-street delay by more than 25%; * adds spill-back anywhere; or * cuts delay at the focus by less than 3% (not worth an officer's time).

docs.title: Why a twin, and which one
docs.body: It is a **cell-transmission model** (Daganzo), the standard macroscopic model of queues and spill-back. It is fast enough to run every candidate over the whole city on the CPU: 30 minutes of Kolkata network v2 (49 junctions, 123 directed links, 5,979 cells) takes 0.12 s, and 20 candidates in one batch take 0.85 s.

docs.title: Why a twin, and which one
docs.body: **Baselines** are evaluated in the same twin and also enter the proposal ranking: * Webster's optimal cycle and split, from the twin's own flows. * Max-pressure control, in its cyclic form so coordination and lost time are kept.

docs.title: The LLM's place
docs.body: The LLM never chooses the timing; the twin and the ranking do. The local tactical LLM (`:8084`, shared with a live system) gets the finished metrics and writes two short sentences in English, then two in Marathi, one call at a time with a 20 s timeout. Each reply is rejected if it: * contains a number that is not in the twin metrics (Western or Marathi digits); * is too long; or * for Marathi, contains stray Latin words or another script.

docs.title: The LLM's place
docs.body: A rejected or missing language falls back to a template that uses only metric numbers. On the box today both languages usually come from the LLM, about 7 s for the pair. The 12B model sometimes emits a garbage token in Marathi, which the check catches.

docs.title: Kolkata at the evening peak (18:00 IST, 45 min horizon, SIMULATED demand)
docs.body: How to read these: * At Park Circus the assumed split is already balanced, so moving green between the roads hurts one more than it helps the other. The gain comes from a shorter cycle, which also breaks coordination with the next signals, and the proposal says so. * The large Red Road gain mostly shows that the generic template does not fit that junction's geometry, not that a real controller is mistimed. That is why proposals at junctions with assumed programs get a lower confidence.

docs.title: Limits
docs.body: * Macroscopic; PCU only; turning ratios assumed; most crossings run an assumed template. * Demand is simulated until the oracle serves Kolkata live state. * Two-phase programs: no protected turns. * The validator checks numbers and script, not meaning.

docs.body: লাইভ পরামর্শ পাওয়া যাচ্ছে না — চিহ্নিত অফলাইন প্রিভিউ দেখানো হচ্ছে।

docs.title: doctrine_note
docs.body: অ্যাম্বুলেন্স প্রতিটি জংশনে পৌঁছনোর 60–180 সেকেন্ড আগে গ্রিন করিডর খোলে।

docs.title: driver_deferred_body
docs.body: কন্ট্রোল রুম এই অনুরোধ স্থগিত রেখেছে — যেখানে আছেন সেখানেই থাকুন, দরকার হলে আবার অনুরোধ করুন।

docs.title: driver_window_unpublished
docs.body: এই ঘটনার উইন্ডো কতক্ষণ, তা জানানো হয়নি — 108 কন্ট্রোলের নির্দেশ মেনে চলুন।

docs.title: comms_session_only
docs.body: খসড়া শুধু এই ব্রাউজার ট্যাবে থাকে — কিছুই পাঠানো হয় না, অডিট রেকর্ডেও লেখা হয় না।

docs.title: strip_watch
docs.body: एक घटना मार्ग सक्रिय है — उसके पास छोटे नियोजित ठहराव संभावित हैं।

docs.title: strip_hold
docs.body: नीचे दिए मार्गों पर नियोजित ठहराव चल रहे हैं। इन्हें दिखाए गए समय पर खोलने की योजना है।

docs.title: strip_severe
docs.body: प्राथमिकता वाला कॉरिडोर ट्रैफ़िक चल रहा है। आम ठहराव छोटे रखने और चौराहे-दर-चौराहे खोलने की योजना है।

docs.title: consequence_procession
docs.body: जुलूस मार्ग पर चल रहा है — गुज़रने तक क्रॉसिंग थोड़ी देर बंद रहती है।

docs.title: consequence_mass_gathering
docs.body: बड़ी भीड़ बिखर रही है — सुरक्षा के लिए ट्रैफ़िक को थोड़ा-थोड़ा छोड़ा जा रहा है।

docs.title: consequence_race
docs.body: कोलकाता मैराथन जैसी सड़क दौड़ चल रही है — अंतिम धावक निकलने तक मार्ग बंद रहेगा।

docs.title: consequence_ceremonial
docs.body: रेड रोड परेड जैसी औपचारिक परेड गुज़र रही है — केवल छोटे क्रमिक ठहराव।

docs.title: consequence_egress_surge
docs.body: स्टेडियम से भीड़ लौट रही है — निकासी लहरों में हो रही है।

docs.title: consequence_work_zone
docs.body: सड़क कार्य से रास्ता सँकड़ा है — एक समय पर एक लेन।

docs.title: consequence_vehicle_pursuit
docs.body: यहाँ पुलिस कार्रवाई चल रही है — अधिकारियों के निर्देश मानें।

docs.title: consequence_unknown
docs.body: एक नियोजित कॉरिडोर कार्रवाई चल रही है — छोटे ठहराव संभावित हैं।

docs.title: card_alt_none
docs.body: मॉडल किए गए मार्गों पर कोई चिह्नित विकल्प नहीं — अतिरिक्त समय रखें।

docs.title: card_alt_unavailable
docs.body: वैकल्पिक मार्ग अभी उपलब्ध नहीं — एक मिनट बाद फिर देखें।

docs.title: citizen_feed_offline
docs.body: लाइव सलाह अभी उपलब्ध नहीं — चिह्नित ऑफ़लाइन पूर्वावलोकन दिख रहा है।

docs.title: doctrine_note
docs.body: ग्रीन कॉरिडोर एम्बुलेंस के चौराहे पहुँचने से ६०–१८० सेकंड पहले खुलता है।

docs.title: driver_deferred_body
docs.body: कंट्रोल रूम ने यह अनुरोध टाल दिया — अपनी जगह रुकें और ज़रूरत हो तो फिर अनुरोध करें।

docs.title: driver_window_unpublished
docs.body: इस घटना के लिए विंडो की अवधि घोषित नहीं — 108 कंट्रोल के निर्देश मानें।

docs.title: comms_session_only
docs.body: ड्राफ़्ट केवल इस ब्राउज़र टैब में रहते हैं — न भेजे जाते हैं, न ऑडिट रिकॉर्ड में लिखे जाते हैं।
